observations.note:
NEAR-MISS, DELIBERATELY NOT COUNTED as instance three of the multi-element temporal composition finding (instances one and two: C04-051#temporal-composition, C04-072#temporal-composition).

WHAT IS SIMILAR. Item C02-07's sentence carries TWO temporal elements: the annotated 'Upon receiving any such notice or upon any such discovery' (RELATIVE_TO_TRIGGER) and a terminal bound, 'until a decision by AMAG has been made whether a Recall or some other corrective action is necessary', which classifies to None on its own (verified by execution). IR v1 holds one temporal, so the terminal bound is unrepresented.

WHY THE MECHANISM IS DIFFERENT, which is the whole reason it is not counted. In instances one and two the surplus bounds sit INSIDE the phrase the model quotes and are SWALLOWED by a greedy '(.+)$' capture, so the candidate COMPILES SILENTLY with a trigger string asserting a wrong window -- that silent misstatement is the finding. Here the terminal bound sits OUTSIDE the annotated temporal phrase entirely: nothing is swallowed, nothing silently misstates the window, and the duration is simply absent from the IR. That is ordinary single-temporal-slot loss, not the greedy-capture defect.

WHY IT IS LOGGED ANYWAY. Padding an instance count with a superficially similar but mechanistically different case would corrupt the very forcing function those instances exist to trigger -- a future ruling session counting three would be reasoning from a contaminated sample. Recorded so the case is FINDABLE and its exclusion is auditable, rather than invisible. Reviewer-confirmed 2026-09-20.
